note: Order every day: item 0 at about 1.12× forecast with a starting buffer, item 1 at about 1.08×, cut back near the end. Main risk: the open-loop stock drifts and shortages pile up on high-demand days.
Order every other day, two days' demand at a time, which halves the fixed 44 fees. Main risk: more holding cost, and capacity gets tight on days when both items arrive.
Order daily with big safety stock (item 0 about 1.3×, item 1 about 1.15×) to keep shortages down. Main risk: write-offs and holding costs, especially for item 1, which costs 12 per unit.
Lean plan: order at forecast level (item 1 at 0.95×). Main risk: true demand averages about 4.6% above forecast, so there will be frequent shortages with penalties and lost margin on item 0.
Put the safety stock on high-margin item 0 (1.2×) and keep item 1 lean (0.8×). Main risk: losing a lot of item 1 sales plus the shortage penalty.
Every other day with large batches (1.3× / 1.15×). Main risk: overflowing the 276-unit warehouse on days when both items arrive (item 1 gets cut off), plus extra write-offs.
Order every three days with three-day batches: lowest fixed cost. Main risk: holding costs grow faster than the fee savings, and stock hits the capacity limit near the peaks.

Build one large buffer at the start, then order daily at about forecast level (1.05× / 1.0×). Main risk: the buffer gets used up halfway through, and after that shortages pile up because demand runs above forecast.
